s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin thickening, joint involvement, and internal organ dysfunction
key_facts: Progressive increase in abdominal girth over the last month
Weight loss of 10 kg over the past 12 months
Skin thickening over the last 5 years
Dry, thickened skin with salt-and-pepper lesions on the face
Hardened and hyperpigmented skin on the limbs
Arthritis in the hands with ulnar deviation of the wrists
Interstitial lung disease on Computed Tomography
Intermediate probability of pulmonary hypertension on Echocardiography
Decreased tear secretion on Schirmer test
Increased collagen and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on skin biopsies

shortlist.label: Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin thickening, joint involvement, and internal organ dysfunction are characteristic of this disease

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of antinuclear antibodies, low Complement C3, and systemic symptoms such as weight loss and fatigue

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of features from systemic sclerosis, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis, including skin thickening, joint involvement, and positive antinuclear antibodies

shortlist.label: Limited Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by skin thickening limited to the hands, feet, and face, with possible internal organ involvement

shortlist.label: Diffuse Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of skin thickening and internal organ involvement, consistent with the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including progressive skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, esophageal dysmotility (solid dysphagia), and interstitial lung disease, are characteristic of systemic sclerosis. The presence of anti-Sm antibody, although weakly positive, and fine speckled antinuclear antibodies, along with elevated inflammatory markers and low complement levels, support this diagnosis. The skin biopsy showing increased collagen and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate further supports systemic sclerosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has some features suggestive of SLE, such as positive antinuclear antibodies and low complement levels, the overall clinical picture, including the prominent skin thickening and esophageal involvement, is more consistent with systemic sclerosis.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: MCTD typically presents with a combination of features from SLE, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis/dermatomyositis. The patient's presentation is more consistent with systemic sclerosis, lacking the high levels of anti-U1-RNP antibodies typically seen in MCTD.

rejected.label: Limited Systemic Sclerosis
rejected.why: The patient's widespread skin involvement and internal organ involvement (e.g., interstitial lung disease, ascites) are not consistent with limited systemic sclerosis, which typically has more restricted skin involvement and fewer internal organ complications.

rejected.label: Diffuse Systemic Sclerosis
rejected.why: While the patient does have diffuse skin involvement, the diagnosis of systemic sclerosis encompasses both limited and diffuse forms, and the specific subtype (diffuse vs. limited) is not as critical as recognizing the disease itself.
